01.actor: Rav and Rabba bar bar Hana
01.event: Rabba bar bar Hana gave Rav money to buy a plot of land for him
01.turn: Rav went and bought the land for himself
01.outcome: Rav owns the land; the Gemara explains he acted because the violent locals would sell only to him and someone else might buy it meanwhile
01.summary: Rabba bar bar Hana gave Rav money and asked him to buy a certain field. Rav went and bought it for himself. The Gemara justifies him: the valley's violent inhabitants respected Rav but not Rabba bar bar Hana, and Rav feared someone else would buy it while he went to report.
01.reason: Two narrated actions (the commission and Rav buying for himself) with a change of ownership and a breach of trust; the Gemara's justification is commentary but the incident itself is told.

02.actor: Rav Pappa, Yehuda bar Mareimar, Abba of Sura
02.event: Rav Pappa goes to write his son's bride's marriage contract; Yehuda bar Mareimar escorts him but will not enter
02.turn: Rav Pappa forces him in; his silence makes Abba of Sura think he is angry, so Abba writes all he owns into the dowry
02.outcome: Yehuda says he did not want this; Abba offers to retract, and Yehuda tells him not to become one who retracts
02.summary: Rav Pappa went to arrange the marriage contract for his son with Abba of Sura's daughter, and Yehuda bar Mareimar escorted him but refused to enter, fearing his presence would pressure the father. Rav Pappa forced him in; he sat silent, and Abba of Sura, thinking him angry, wrote all his possessions into the dowry. Yehuda said he had not wanted it; Abba offered to retract, and Yehuda told him to keep his word.
02.reason: Multiple actions (escort, forcing him in, silence, writing the dowry) with causality and a clear change; a full story.

03.event: a superintendent refuses to rent his domain to his neighbors for an eiruv
03.turn: they ask Rav Yehuda bar Oshaya and Rav Mattana whether they may rent from his wife; neither knows
03.outcome: Rav Yehuda tells them, citing Shmuel, that a man's wife may make an eiruv without his knowledge
03.summary: A superintendent living near Rav Yehuda bar Oshaya refused to rent his domain to his neighbors. They went from sage to sage asking whether they could rent it from his wife, until Rav Yehuda ruled, citing Shmuel, that they could.
03.missing: whether they then rented from the wife; the outcome is only implied
03.reason: There is a real event (the refusal) and a search across several rabbis, but it ends in a ruling with no narrated change; the refusal and the rounds of asking keep it slightly above a bare case-and-ruling, so borderline rather than not.

04.missing: any event beyond Minyamin's report of his own marriage and his stated plan for his son
04.reason: A baraita cited as evidence: Minyamin reports what he did and intends to do; nothing follows and no one responds.

05.actor: Rabbi Abba bar Shumni and Rav Menashya bar Yirmeya
05.event: parting at the ford of the Yofti River
05.turn: they agree each will say a teaching the other has not heard
05.summary: Two sages parting at a river ford agreed that each would say a teaching the other had not heard, and each did so.
05.missing: any event beyond the setting and the exchange of teachings
05.reason: A setting followed by teaching; teaching is speech and there is no conflict, and a setting that only frames the teaching is not the second event (Shabbat 147a). Segments 5-7 are further legal discussion.

06.event: Levi publicly expounded Rabbi's ruling in Rabbi's name and was not praised
06.turn: he expounded it in the name of the many
06.summary: Levi went out and taught a ruling in Rabbi's name and the audience did not praise him; when he taught it as the majority view, they praised him. The Gemara infers the halakha follows Rabbi.
06.reason: There is a reaction and a change, but the acts are teaching, which is speech; mainly speech with something happening fits borderline shape 1.

07.missing: the incident itself; the passage is only Rabbi Elazar's question to an elder about when a past court permitted a woman to remarry
07.reason: A question, with an earlier ruling only presupposed; there is no narrated event and the incident is not even sketched enough to count as alluded under R-C6.

08.missing: any event beyond Rav Pappa instructing someone how to sign
08.reason: A bare report of a ruling Rav Pappa gave, cited as precedent; nothing follows.

09.event: they would go to eat the fruits of Genosar; Rabbi Yohanan would eat enormous quantities
09.outcome: he would swear he had not tasted nourishment
09.summary: Rabba bar bar Hana recounts that when they followed Rabbi Yohanan to eat Genosar fruit, Rabbi Yohanan would eat huge amounts and swear he had not tasted anything nourishing.
09.missing: a one-time event or change; it is a habitual description
09.reason: A habitual practice cited as evidence about the word for nourishment; the custom leads nowhere, so it stays a report.

10.event: Ravina examined a slaughterer's knife in Babylonia in his teacher Rav Ashi's lifetime
10.outcome: Ravina defended himself as a disciple-colleague, citing Rav Hamnuna's precedent
10.summary: Ravina examined a slaughterer's knife while Rav Ashi was alive, and Rav Ashi asked why he had done so. Ravina cited Rav Hamnuna's practice and argued that, as a disciple-colleague, he could rule outside his teacher's town.
10.reason: One real act (examining the knife) followed by a dialogue of justification; mainly speech with an event, which is borderline shape 1. Segments 2-3 are bare reports of practice.

11.event: in an incident, Rabbi ruled according to the Rabbis of the mishna
11.turn: Perata objected that this would leave the court no advantage
11.outcome: Rabbi reversed his ruling (or, in Rav Safra's version, did not carry it out)
11.summary: Rav Dimi reported that in an incident, Rabbi ruled like the Rabbis of the mishna. Perata objected that then the court would have no advantage, and Rabbi reversed his decision. Rav Safra's version has Rabbi refrain before acting.
11.missing: the facts of the underlying case
11.reason: There is a ruling, an objection and a reversal, which is a change, but the case itself is only alluded to and the action is all ruling and speech; borderline.

12.missing: any one-time event; it describes Rav Huna's habitual demand
12.reason: A custom (what Rav Huna would say to litigants) cited as illustration, leading to nothing.

13.missing: any event; it is a remark by Levi and reports of sages' practice and opinion
13.reason: Speech and habitual practices cited as legal evidence; no event and no change.

14.actor: Rabbi Abbahu, Rabbi Elai and those seeking Abbahu
14.turn: they ask Rabbi Elai where he is
14.outcome: Rabbi Elai answers in a riddle that he has consulted the Nasi and gone south
14.summary: People asked Rabbi Elai to show them where Rabbi Abbahu was hiding, and he answered cryptically that Abbahu had taken counsel with the Nasi and gone south.
14.missing: why Abbahu hid and what followed; the event is only alluded to
14.reason: Mainly clever speech, with a real event (Abbahu's flight) only alluded to; between borderline and not, so borderline.

15.missing: any event beyond Ravina's collection of a dowry, cited as proof
15.reason: A report of how Ravina ruled and collected, cited as a legal proof; there is no other narrated action or change.

16.missing: any event beyond Rava bar Avuh collecting on two notes, cited as proof
16.reason: A precedent cited as evidence and then debated; a bare report of an act inside legal discussion.

17.event: a man gives Shmuel a hand as he leaves a ferry
17.turn: Shmuel asks his business; the man says he has a case
17.outcome: Shmuel disqualifies himself from judging it
17.summary: Shmuel was crossing on a ferry, and a man helped him out with his hand. When Shmuel asked what he was doing there, the man said he had a case for him, and Shmuel declared himself disqualified from judging it.
17.reason: Two actions with causality and a change: the man's favour leads Shmuel to recuse himself; the recusal is an act, not a bare ruling.

18.event: Rav Yosef has taught a ruling in Rabbi's name
18.turn: Rav Beivai tells the sages not to listen: he himself told it to Rav Yosef in Rav Adda bar Ahava's name
18.outcome: Rav Yosef exclaims that he confused 'Rabbi' with 'many'
18.summary: Rav Beivai told the sages not to heed Rav Yosef's attribution, because he had taught it to him in Rav Adda bar Ahava's name and with a different reading. Rav Yosef exclaimed that he had mistaken 'rabbim' for 'Rabbi'.
18.reason: All speech, but with conflict (a public correction) and a change (Rav Yosef realizes his error); speech with conflict is borderline.

19.event: a man who made an eiruv with onions to reach Tiv'in comes before Rabbi Meir in Ardiska on Shabbat
19.turn: Rabbi Meir rules his eiruv invalid
19.outcome: Rabbi Meir confines him to his four cubits
19.summary: Rabbi Meir spent Shabbat in Ardiska, and a man came to him saying he had made an eiruv with onions to walk to Tiv'in. Rabbi Meir made him stay within his four cubits.
19.reason: One event (coming before him with the eiruv) and a ruling, but the ruling is an act that changes the man's situation (he is confined), which keeps it borderline rather than not (Ketubot 65a).

20.missing: any event; it is a question and an answer
20.reason: A dialogue between Rav Hisda and his daughter, with no event and no conflict.
